svg.title: How to read the H–x chart for H2SO4/H2O
svg.text: How to read the H–x chart for H₂SO₄/H₂O (SVNA Fig. 12.17)
Enthalpy of the solution (kJ per kg solution) against mass % H₂SO₄; isotherms −20 … 140 °C; redrawn
Find the composition on the bottom axis (here 60 wt% H₂SO₄) and go straight up.
Stop at the isotherm of the solution temperature (here 60 °C; interpolate between isotherms if needed).
Go horizontally to the left (H) axis.
Read the enthalpy: here H ≈ −200 kJ/kg solution (datum: liquid water at 0 °C and H₂SO₄ at 25 °C = 0).
Mixing two streams adiabatically: the mixture lies on the straight line joining them (lever rule); its isotherm gives T.
A point above the dotted boiling line is a boiling liquid + vapour; below the freezing lines solid separates.
Redrawn from SVNA Fig. 12.17 (digitized curves); in the exam read the printed chart — values may differ slightly.
